scope: October 19 creative-AI edition, updated by the October 20 daily review. Three October 19 submissions were newly discovered in today’s arXiv listing; submission times precede the previous review. Ming Tiny serving documentation changed after that review. Retained weekly items and September weight dates are explicitly dated. Scoped author/vendor claims, no independent reproduction. No robotics or physical AI.

papers.title: Mise-en-Video: block the shot in 3D before generating it.
papers.full_title: Mise-en-Video: Fine-Grained 3D Control for Multi-Shot Video Generation
papers.change: New research extends multi-shot control from 2D placement to oriented 3D staging; not a verified Kling product rollout. Submitted October 19; newly discovered in the October 20 arXiv listing after the previous review, not an October 20 launch.
papers.summary: Projects colored NOCS boxes into per-frame orientation maps and injects them through ControlDiT. Hierarchical attention separates global, shot and subject text. Trained on 160K annotated videos with a 1B backbone.
papers.evaluation: Author evaluation: 100 multi-shot prompts. Orientation mAOE 0.2015 radians versus 0.4094 for MultiShotMaster and 0.4079 for EchoShot. The 14B HoloCine baseline remains better on several consistency and aesthetic metrics; no universal SOTA claim.
papers.caveat: Backbone capacity limits dynamic-video quality. Reusing an identity description across separately generated edits does not ensure the same identity.
papers.access: Full paper reviewed. Official project retrieval failed; code, weights and license not verified. No inference run.
papers.creator_implication: A promising direction for explicit actor placement, facing and cross-shot blocking.
papers.visual_angle: Proposed analytic director desk: drag and rotate colored 3D actor boxes; switch cameras across three shots; inspect projected coordinate-color maps and subject/shot/global attention masks. Compare equal 2D rectangles with different facing directions. This illustrates conditioning, not generated footage.
papers.review_depth: Primary method, evaluation tables, limitations, submission history; project access failure recorded.

papers.title: Wan-Alpha++: animate the asset, including its disappearance.
papers.full_title: Wan-Alpha++: Animating a Single RGBA Asset into Controllable Transparent Video Effects
papers.change: New image-conditioned extension of earlier Wan-Alpha; the original text-to-RGBA model is not new. Submitted October 19; newly discovered in the October 20 arXiv listing after the previous review, not an October 20 launch.
papers.summary: Temporal phase reparameterization moves visible content to conditioning boundaries, then restores the transparent-visible-transparent effect. Uses Wan2.1-I2V-14B with shared RGBA latents and transparent-state guidance.
papers.evaluation: Authors evaluate 60 image-conditioned videos, with 81 frames at 480×832 and 40 sampling steps. Effect-reference DINO-I rises 0.6679→0.9227 against Wan2.1-FLF2V plus MatAnyone. Appearance metrics include only sufficiently visible frames. Forty participants rank effects.
papers.caveat: Small curated effect training set: 196 clips. Comparisons target selected two-stage generation/matting baselines, not all commercial VFX tools. Four-step text-to-RGBA results do not describe the new 40-step image-conditioned path.
papers.access: Paper available. Official predecessor repository still lists I2V weights as unchecked; released v1/v2 T2V artifacts do not establish ++ availability. Commit-history retrieval returned 429. No new weights or inference verified.
papers.creator_implication: Potentially useful for compositable smoke, glow or magical effects with an explicit reference asset.
papers.visual_angle: Proposed analytic alpha timeline: scrub an effect fading in/out, drag the visible reference frame and phase offset, and switch checkerboard or colored backgrounds. Show original versus shifted timelines and reconstruct the final composite. Teach why an empty first frame carries little appearance information.
papers.review_depth: Primary method/evaluation/history and official predecessor README/project inspected; no new model execution.

papers.title: FluidGen: teach the smoke model what moves, not just what it looks like.
papers.full_title: FluidGen: Physics-Aware Fluid Video Generation via Motion-Guided Post-Training
papers.change: New generative VFX research for smoke, fire and explosions; fits filmmaking rather than robotics. Submitted October 19; newly discovered in the October 20 arXiv listing after the previous review, not an October 20 launch.
papers.summary: A Wan2.1-I2V-14B extension jointly predicts RGB and pixel-aligned 3D velocity. Simulation-supervised motion supports velocity-based DPO rewards.
papers.evaluation: Author tests: 15 FluidNexus sequences and 20 in-the-wild images. Final FVD 199.2 versus base Wan 569.7; supervised-only 192.1. DPO improves VBench imaging quality 0.4282→0.4627 while PSNR and subject consistency decline slightly.
papers.caveat: Small selected evaluation; no independent reproduction or broad current-model ranking. Reward scores physical plausibility rather than enforcing Navier–Stokes. Predicted physical velocity and the latent flow-matching velocity are different quantities. Artist control of predicted velocity is future work.
papers.access: Official project explicitly marks code and data as coming soon; no weights or runnable release verified.
papers.creator_implication: Research direction for coherent fluid VFX; project shows keyframe-guided smoke transformations and Houdini transfer demonstrations, not independently tested production reliability.
papers.visual_angle: Proposed analytic smoke lab: advect colored density through a 2D velocity field; expose curl, divergence, viscosity and timestep, plus arrow/color encodings. Contrast physical scene motion with a separate latent flow trajectory. Add a reward-versus-fidelity panel to explain DPO tradeoffs. Label as a numerical teaching simulation, not FluidGen inference.
papers.review_depth: Primary method/evaluation/ablations/conclusion/history and official project status verified.

papers.version: 19 Oct code release; 20 Oct serving documentation
papers.title: Ming-3.0 TTS: voice controls are task-specific; streaming is a separate promise
papers.summary: Public inference code exposes voice design, reference-voice synthesis and delivery controls in separate task modes. Tiny adds scripted multi-speaker dialogue. A new model-card change documents SGLang-Omni serving.
papers.change: Code's initial commit is October 19 at 08:58 UTC, missed in the previous review. Both checkpoints were uploaded September 24, so these are not new October weights. Tiny's serving-instructions commit is October 20 at 03:27 UTC, after the last review.
papers.evaluation: Author tables cover Seed-TTS, selected multilingual subsets, NVBench, emotion and voice-design tasks. Tiny's Korean CER is 6.000%, versus 0.5B's 1.728%; speaker similarity and expression accuracy vary by task. The repository repeats independent-leaderboard ranks, but the live leaderboard was not retrieved here, so no independently verified rank is asserted.
papers.caveat: Controls cannot be combined arbitrarily. SGLang-Omni's documented endpoint returns a complete waveform even with stream=true; this is not incremental low-latency playback. Its simple TTS/cloning interface does not establish parity with every reference-repository task. No latency, listening or generation test was run.
papers.access: Public inference repository and both checkpoint listings verified; repository license and model-card metadata say MIT. Tiny’s Ling V3 backbone has 7.9B total parameters, about 1.3B active per token; active count is not resident checkpoint size. No weights downloaded. Tiny's card and current repository disagree on whether freeform requires a reference; the pinned task contract marks it optional, so callers should follow the chosen implementation.
papers.creator_implication: A new self-hostable candidate for expressive narration and dialogue. Test delivery, speaker similarity and time to first playable audio separately.
papers.review_depth: Public GitHub/HF commit APIs, pinned task contract, model cards and official serving cookbook; no execution.

papers.title: ResStreamGS: stop sending the whole scene every frame.
papers.full_title: ResStreamGS: Residual-Sensitive Dual-Stream Gaussian Splatting for Mobile Volumetric Video Streaming
papers.summary: Caches stable splats per frame group; updates attribute-sensitive splats frame by frame.
papers.change: October 15 v1, covered in the October 16 delta and carried into this weekly synthesis with a new original interactive. Not a new October 19 release.
papers.evaluation: Author tests: six 300-frame sequences, held-out cameras, 20-frame groups. Against a controlled V3-style baseline: +7.51–8.35 dB PSNR and 21.4–56.5% lower amortized payload. 30.883 FPS on one Snapdragon 778G phone.
papers.caveat: Payload is not wireless performance. Culling and pruning also improve speed. Abrupt changes challenge fixed groups; GIFStream has smaller payloads.
papers.access: Full paper reviewed; implementation not verified, no reproduction.
papers.creator_implication: For captured volumetric scenes. Stationary splats can still need appearance updates.
papers.review_depth: Primary methods, evaluation, ablations and submission history.

papers.title: TriFold: give irregular Gaussian scenes a regular latent space
papers.full_title: TriFold: Folding irregular 3D Gaussians into structured latents for 3D Scene Generation
papers.summary: A native Gaussian VAE maps variable-size scenes to triplane latents. Multiple learned slots preserve information when primitives collide in a projected cell; occupancy and set decoding recover adaptive local counts. A latent flow model supports point-cloud or single-image conditioning.
papers.change: New to the archive this week. Original submission October 16; an October 19 aggregator date is not a revision.
papers.evaluation: Author tests on InteriorGS and Aria/SceneSplat: approximately 19,600 crops plus 8,600 scenes, split before cropping. Reconstruction reports 26.55 dB PSNR versus GaussianGPT's 21.40 under the adapted common protocol. Generation is assessed within its own conditioning setup, without a matched cross-generator comparison.
papers.caveat: Limited indoor-scene diversity and fixed physical crop scale constrain generalization. Unseen areas are plausible completions, not recovered truth. The local candidate count remains bounded; adaptive does not mean unlimited.
papers.access: Paper available. Official project page retrieval failed; code, weights and license availability not verified.
papers.creator_implication: Relevant to generating explorable 3D set pieces from partial views, with a clear distinction between observed and invented geometry.
papers.review_depth: Primary full method, evaluation, appendix limitations; no execution

papers.title: MOSS-Image: give the renderer a layout
papers.summary: A 5B DiT combines text and layout conditioning with an optional external prompt planner. Structured boxes make composition an explicit input.
papers.change: Official repository dates Base/SFT code-and-weight release October 16. Paper v1 was submitted October 16; the repository's October 19 news entry announces arXiv availability, not a separate new model release.
papers.evaluation: Authors report 96.3 Mean-6 on LLTB: 240 English/Chinese text tasks, four images each, all scored. The OCR multiset-recall metric ignores order and does not directly penalize extra text. RLA uses 61 design tasks and blind human preferences; MOSS ranks second among displayed end-to-end systems with an external planner. These are author-run evaluations, not an independent reproduction.
papers.caveat: Current backbone is text-to-image, with no direct reference-image conditioning or image editing. Layout changes regenerate an image. The external planner can introduce factual/design errors. General superiority and reliable typesetting are unestablished.
papers.access: Public Base/SFT weights and inference code verified; SFT model card explicitly licenses weights and bundled inference code Apache-2.0. No generation run. Official defaults: 50 Euler steps, CFG 3, shift 5, negative-branch layer 22 skipping; 5B excludes the separate frozen 9B text encoder.
papers.creator_implication: A practical candidate for editable poster/storyboard layout specifications. Review the rendered wording, not just visual appeal or OCR coverage.
papers.controls: Drag colored text/object boxes; edit exact strings and line breaks; change canvas ratio; toggle centered-pixel versus normalized coordinate display. Show bbox conversion and overlap, not invented generated outputs.
papers.misconception: A high text-coverage score means every string is correct and in the right order.
papers.visual_status: Proposed analytic layout/metric explainer; no MOSS inference built or run.
papers.review_depth: Read primary history, method, evaluation and limitations, plus evaluation appendix, official guide and SFT card.

papers.title: Instant Soundtracks: keep music and effects editable.
papers.summary: Video-conditioned music and timed effects arrive with separate editable tracks and optional reference to the video's existing audio.
papers.change: October 15 release, carried into the weekly list from October 16's delta. Article updated October 19; no second launch inferred.
papers.evaluation: Official feature announcement and API contract, with no quantitative synchronization benchmark or independent output test in this review.
papers.caveat: Detection of a visual event does not guarantee perfect audio timing. API add_sfx, separate_tracks and use_audio_as_reference all default false; enabling separate tracks returns a ZIP.
papers.access: Vendor says available in ElevenCreative, ElevenMusic and API. API accepts up to ten videos, 200 MB and 600 seconds combined. No paid request or generation run.
papers.creator_implication: Score an assembled edit, then correct effects or swap music without remaking the video. Compare event timing and sound quality separately.
papers.review_depth: Launch publication/update dates, current product listing and API flags/limits verified.
